revenge.label: The urge for revenge
revenge.insight: The Quran acknowledges the right of the one wronged: “And if you punish, punish with an equivalent of that with which you were harmed,” but it sets “the equivalent” as the ceiling and encourages something higher: “But if you are patient — it is better for those who are patient.” The Prophet ﷺ “never took revenge for himself, unless something sacred to Allah was violated,” and at al-Ta'if he refused to have those who harmed him destroyed, saying: “Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their descendants people who worship Allah.” Claiming your right through lawful means is not revenge.

now: Do not act now; revenge is usually a decision people regret
Write down what you want to do, then ask: does it go beyond “the equivalent”? Does it please Allah?
week: Turn the urge for revenge into a lawful claim for your right (a complaint, the courts, a mediator)
Leave the wrongdoer to Allah: “And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do”
long: Work on healing your wound instead of being busy hurting someone else

questions: Will revenge give me back what I lost?
How will I see myself in a year's time if I take revenge?
avoid: Taking justice into your own hands outside the law
Defaming or lying about your opponent
Going beyond the equivalent

suspicion.label: Suspicion and judging intentions
suspicion.insight: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech.” The Prophet ﷺ rebuked Usamah when he judged a man's intention: “Did you cut open his heart?” The way is to judge by what is apparent, to verify reports (“investigate”), and to interpret people's words in the best possible way.

now: Write down three alternative explanations for the person's behaviour other than the bad one
week: Ask the person kindly what they meant instead of assuming
long: Train yourself in “the believing men and believing women thinking good of one another”

questions: What real evidence is there of their intention?
Am I interpreting their behaviour through an old wound?
avoid: Spying to confirm a suspicion
Acting on the basis of suspicion

gossip.label: Backbiting and gossip
gossip.insight: Backbiting is “your mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes,” and the Quran depicts it in the ugliest image: “Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead?” The Prophet ﷺ described the Muslim as the one “from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.” And if you are the one being backbitten, you have in “So exalt with praise of your Lord and be of those who prostrate” a remedy for a tight chest, and your good deeds grow by what they take from their own.

now: If you backbit someone: stop, seek forgiveness, and mention the person well in that same gathering
If they backbite you: do not get caught up replying to every word
week: Leave gatherings of backbiting politely, or change the subject
If someone passes on gossip to you, do not act on it without verifying
long: Make your rule: “say what is good or keep silent”

questions: Would I have said this in front of them?
Why do I feel the need to talk about others?
avoid: Carrying tales between people
Answering backbiting with backbiting

slander.label: False accusation and reputation
slander.insight: The incident of the slander is the greatest example: pure ‘A'ishah was accused, was patient and said “so patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one sought for help,” until her innocence came down from heaven, and Allah said: “Do not think it bad for you; rather it is good for you.” Jurayj was accused, and he made wudu and prayed before defending himself. The way is patience, steadfastness, calm and lawful self-defence, and leaving one's vindication to Allah — while keeping the wronged person's right to claim their due (“Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged”).

now: Do not reply in anger; make wudu and pray two units of prayer
Gather the facts and the evidence calmly
week: Clarify your position once, clearly, to those concerned
If the damage is serious, consult a legal professional
long: Trust that the truth comes out, and carry on with your life and work

questions: Whose opinion really matters to me?
Will replying put the rumour out, or spread it further?
avoid: Answering a rumour with a counter-rumour
Withdrawing completely because of what people say
triggers: blamed for something i didn't do

neighbors.label: Neighbours
neighbors.insight: “Jibril kept enjoining me to treat the neighbour well, until I thought he would make him an heir.” Being good to neighbours is part of faith, and harming them diminishes faith. With a harmful neighbour, the Prophet ﷺ taught a gradual approach: patience first, then a clever solution that draws on legitimate social pressure without aggression.

now: Start with a calm, direct conversation with the neighbour
week: Offer a gift or a kind gesture before complaining
Involve a third party if the harm continues
long: Use official channels if needed, without aggression

questions: Does my neighbour know that they are bothering me?
avoid: Responding with similar harm
Cutting off completely

work.label: Work and the workplace
work.insight: In Islam, work becomes worship through intention (“actions are only by intentions”) and is a trust (“Allah loves that when one of you does a piece of work, he does it with excellence”). The Quran's standard for a worker is “the strong, the trustworthy.” Whoever is wronged at work has the right to claim his due (“whoever avenges himself after having been wronged — those have not upon them any cause for blame”), while being just even with those you dislike (“do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just”). Your work is seen by Allah even if the manager does not see it: “Do as you will, for Allah will see your deeds.”

now: Separate your feelings about the person from your assessment of the situation
Calmly document the facts (dates, messages, achievements)
week: Speak directly to the person concerned in calm, professional language
If that does not work, use the official channels (HR, a higher manager)
Renew your intention: I work for Allah, then for my livelihood
long: Develop your competence (“the strong”) and protect your reputation (“the trustworthy”)
If the environment is persistently harmful, look for an alternative with planning, not in anger

questions: Is the problem the person or the system?
What can I control in this situation?
Do I need to stay here, or is it time for a change?
avoid: Resigning in a moment of anger
Backbiting and taking sides at work
Underperforming to get back at the manager

leadership.label: Leadership and managing a team
leadership.insight: Prophetic leadership combines gentleness and firmness: “So by mercy from Allah, you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah.” He consulted his wife at the most delicate moment, led by example when the team did not respond, was just even with those closest to him (“if Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad were to steal”), and was considerate of the weak (“Are you one who puts people to trial, O Mu‘adh?”).

now: Before any difficult decision, listen to your team's opinion
If the team makes a mistake, correct without humiliating
week: Lead by example: do yourself what you ask of others
Review the fairness of how tasks and recognition are distributed
long: Build a culture of consultation followed by decisiveness
Give workers their rights “before their sweat dries”

questions: Does my team feel safe enough to tell me the truth?
Do I treat everyone by the same standard?
avoid: Harshness and public reprimand
Favouritism
Making decisions without consultation

rizq.label: Provision and money worries
rizq.insight: Provision is guaranteed by Allah (“and in the heaven is your provision”), but it is sought through effort (“so walk among its slopes”), like the birds that “go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening.” Its keys in the Quran and Sunnah are: piety (“whoever fears Allah — He will make for him a way out and will provide for him from where he does not expect”), seeking forgiveness (“He will send rain from the sky upon you in continuing showers and give you increase in wealth”), gratitude (“if you are grateful, I will surely increase you”), keeping ties of kinship (“whoever would like his provision to be increased, let him keep the ties of kinship”), and lawful work however humble.

now: Write your budget: income, essential expenses, what can be reduced
Repeat: “O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me independent by Your bounty of all besides You”
week: Set fixed hours every day to look for work or a source of income
Seek forgiveness often, and keep ties with your relatives
Do not look down on temporary lawful work
long: Develop a skill that is in demand

questions: Is my worry about having too little money, or about managing it badly?
What available means have I not taken yet?
avoid: Turning to the unlawful (interest, cheating) under the pressure of need
Envying those who have been given more
Passively waiting for relief without effort

debt.label: Debt
debt.insight: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge from “the burden of debt and being overpowered by men,” and he promised: “Whoever takes people's money intending to repay it, Allah will repay it on his behalf.” The way is: a sincere intention to repay, no delaying while able (“delay by a wealthy person is injustice”), asking for more time and for intercession (as he did with the creditors of Jabir's father), organising what you have, and supplication.

now: Write a complete list of your debts: amount, creditor, due date
Repeat: “O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me independent by Your bounty of all besides You”
week: Contact your creditors honestly and ask for a repayment schedule
Stop taking on any new, unnecessary debt
Ask an experienced or respected person to mediate for you
long: A repayment plan that starts with the smallest or the most costly debt
Avoid interest-based loans to pay off other debts

questions: Am I borrowing out of necessity, or to keep up with others?
What could I sell or do without?
avoid: Avoiding your creditors and lying to them
Borrowing with interest
Despairing and collapsing
debt.help: For large debts or legal matters, consult a financial or legal professional.

poverty.label: Poverty and need
poverty.insight: Poverty takes nothing from a believer's dignity: the Prophet ﷺ lived for days without a fire being lit in his house, and Abu Hurayrah tied a stone over his stomach. True wealth is “the richness of the soul,” and “successful is the one who has accepted Islam, has been provided with what is sufficient, and whom Allah has made content.” Alongside this comes the command to strive (“it is better for any of you to take a rope…”), and the person in need should not feel ashamed to ask for help with dignity.

now: Do not be ashamed to ask for help from charities or relatives, with dignity
Pray: “My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need”
week: Look for any lawful work, however simple
Make use of the social programmes available in your country
long: Develop a skill that opens a door of provision
Contentment does not mean giving up effort

questions: Who can help me right now?
What blessings do I still have?
avoid: The unlawful, under the pressure of need
Despair and isolation
